entries.issuing_body: OCC, Federal Reserve Board, FDIC and NCUA
entries.title: Interagency proposed third-party risk management guidance published in the Federal Register; comments due November 16, 2026
entries.facts: The OCC, the Federal Reserve Board, the FDIC and the NCUA published proposed interagency guidance on third-party risk management in the Federal Register on September 15, 2026, at 91 FR 58536 (document number 2026-18859), under docket numbers OCC-2026-0793, OP-1881 and NCUA-2026-1684. The document states that comments must be received on or before November 16, 2026. The proposal would replace the 2023 Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships and its related supplemental resources with a risk-based approach tailored to a banking organization's size, complexity and risk profile. The document states that the proposed guidance would encourage responsible innovation, consistent with Executive Order 14405, by removing broad-based and overly prescriptive language from the 2023 guidance that may unduly impede fintechs from entering partnerships with banking organizations, and it refers to fintechs that partner with banking organizations to provide access to financial services.
entries.source_label: Federal Register — Proposed Third-Party Risk Management Guidance, 91 FR 58536 (Sept. 15, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: fintechs partnering with banks, banking-as-a-service providers, payment processors, bank vendor and compliance teams

entries.issuing_body: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
entries.title: Federal Reserve publishes a proposed third-party risk management guide for traditional community banking organizations; comments due November 16, 2026
entries.facts: The Federal Reserve Board published a proposed third-party risk management guide for traditional community banking organizations in the Federal Register on September 15, 2026, at 91 FR 58438 (document number 2026-18852, docket OP-1880). The document states that comments must be received on or before November 16, 2026. The guide is a companion to the interagency third-party risk management guidance published the same day and is addressed to community banking organizations with less than $30 billion in assets. It describes categories of third party commonly used by such institutions, including core processors, payment processing and digital banking providers delivering wire transfers, ACH, mobile banking and treasury management, card issuers, BSA/AML platforms, fraud prevention tools, cybersecurity vendors, IT infrastructure providers and loan management systems, and states that it establishes no enforceable standards. The document states that the proposed guide is not intended for community banking organizations with more complex business models or third-party relationship profiles, such as complex bank-fintech partnerships.
entries.source_label: Federal Register — Proposed Third-Party Risk Management Guide for Traditional Community Banking Organizations, 91 FR 58438 (Sept. 15, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: payment processors, card issuers, core and digital banking providers, BSA/AML and fraud vendors serving community banks

entries.title: CFTC whistleblower award final rule published in the Federal Register, effective October 16, 2026
entries.facts: The CFTC final rule 'Whistleblower Award Determination' (RIN 3038-AF74) was published in the Federal Register on September 16, 2026, at 91 FR 58576 (document number 2026-19006), amending 17 CFR part 165. The document states that the rule is effective October 16, 2026. The rule establishes a 30 percent presumption under which a whistleblower meeting the stated conditions receives the statutory maximum of 30 percent of monetary sanctions where the total award would not exceed $5 million, unless factors warranting reduction such as culpability or unreasonable reporting delay are present. The release states the change is intended to reduce claim processing delays, which it describes as having historically averaged over 2.5 years, by removing the individualized factor-by-factor review previously applied to claims of every size, and makes technical corrections reflecting the 2025 transfer of the Whistleblower Office to the Office of the General Counsel.
entries.source_label: Federal Register — Whistleblower Award Determination, 91 FR 58576 (Sept. 16, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: CFTC registrants, designated contract markets, futures commission merchants, crypto derivatives and event-contract exchanges, compliance and legal teams
